raw_response:
I've farmed this 2 mu plot for 45 years, and at 68 I know its characteristics precisely — where the soil compacts, where it dries faster, how the groundwater table shifts in a dry spring. My wife and I handle everything ourselves. Hired labor makes no economic sense on 2 mu, and frankly the physical work keeps us from rusting shut. I studied at agricultural college, so I approach management systematically, but I've learned that textbook rates need adjustment for a smallholder's cash flow and an old man's back. A bad fall would cost 50,000 yuan at the hospital; avoiding that is worth more than an extra 50 kg of grain.

I'm planting single-crop spring maize, sowing around April 25th when the 5-day average soil temperature stabilizes above 10°C. Double-cropping wheat and maize is too labor-intensive for us now, and the machinery fixed costs for wheat on 2 mu are prohibitive. I'm using Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — about 2.5 kg per mu at roughly 50 yuan per mu. I've used this variety for a decade; it's reliable and I understand its growth pattern under our conditions.

For nutrient management, I'm targeting a yield of 480 kg per mu, which requires roughly 16 kg N per mu based on the uptake curve. I'll apply a base dressing of 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting — that delivers 6 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 6 kg K₂O. At jointing I'll topdress 20 kg per mu of urea for an additional 9 kg N. I don't split phosphorus or potassium — there's no agronomic justification for that on maize. Some extension bulletins recommend 20 kg N per mu, but I'm conservative at 15 kg N total; the marginal return above that on this soil isn't worth the cash outlay when you're living on a pension and 2 mu of grain.

Irrigation will be twice: one light irrigation after planting to ensure uniform emergence, and one critical irrigation at tasseling–silking in late July. Pumping costs are metered and run about 40–50 yuan per mu per irrigation, so I monitor soil moisture carefully. I'll use furrow irrigation from the tube well — flood irrigation wastes water and the village meters every cubic meter.

Weed control is one pre-emergence application of atrazine plus acetochlor. I scout for corn borer weekly, but unless I see frass or egg masses I don't spray insecticide — integrated pest management isn't just for large farms.

Tillage is single-pass rotary tillage with a 15-horsepower walking tractor. I pay a neighbor 80 yuan to do the 2 mu. I used to do it myself, but at 68 the vibration is hard on my hands.

Total input costs come to about 750 yuan. Expected output is 960 kg at roughly 2.2 yuan per kg, so about 2,100 yuan gross. That's roughly 1,350 yuan net, plus we keep 200 kg for our own consumption and chicken feed. At my age the objective isn't maximization — it's sustainable management without injury or debt.
